It's not everyday I can say that I am not only impressed by a free to play game, but that I really enjoy it too. The First Descendant has been an incredibly pleasant surprise in many ways.

Graphics look beautiful with realistic lighting, nice textures and shading and smooth performance with options for upscaling like DLSS available.

I'm a big gun guy, so it was pretty important to me that the effects of the firearms were somewhat accurate, even for a fantasy game. The guns in this game sound punchy and heavy - like they actually weigh something, and pack a sizeable punch. 

The environments are also quite nice. As you play the story missions you'll travel through various biomes - each with their own look and feel. There's dungeons and boss fights too - which are pretty awesome. The boss fights themselves can be pretty epic (known as void intercepts) with bosses having various degrees of level and difficulty, weak points and abilities to contest against.

And then there are the characters. Omg. Never seen to much T & A in a game before but it's here, and if you are are looking for a virtual waifu that kicks ass there's a good chance you'll find one here. 

There are some downsides however. The game can feel quite grindy at times. There are microtransactions in place, and utilising them can yield accelerated progression, which I am also not a huge fan of considering it seems like the game is as grindy as it it to accommodate such boosts. And there are SOME missions that are absolutely infuriating, such as one about an old camp where you have to traverse a bunch of treehouses and collect these orbs. If I wanted to play a platforming game, I would do that. I came here for action, and these mission types completely take you out of it and ruin your experience until you can get past them.

The nice thing is, like many things in the game, you CAN do these missions with others in  public matchmaking which will allow you to complete them faster. I do also like that many activities, including dungeons, can be done solo, even though the game requires an internet connection. 

Overall I am really having a good time with this game and hope to enjoy it for years to come.

The First Descendant (henceforth: TFD) can be considered as a looter shooter experience like Destinity 2 (henceforth: D2) and Warframe (henceforth: WF), however, obviously there are differences. First of all, observe that I compare TFD (the newbie) with the granddaddies of the genre (D2 and WF) - I do this because it holds up against those very well.

Combat: Both D2 and TFD focus on a shooter experience and both do it damn well. WF reaches out in to other styles of engagements to an extend that it might get annoying (from sneaking into spaceships, submarine/mech/shapeship battles) and is poisoned by ... fishing, mining, etc. The common denominator of all three, the shooter experience, feels worst in WF and in my opinion best in TFD.

Missions: I do not go to deep into that because in the very end, they do not matter that much in either game. They all have defense, extermination, bosses, ... important is the combat because if you do not like the combat, then you will not enjoy any mission. It is important to realize that even the normal non-boss missions in TFD  can be challenging if you  do not build your char properly. If you build your char properly, then it is a piece of cake. Same holds for selecting the right missions for farming etc. play smart, this cuts down the time to getting new chars to a few days or less.

Raiding/Bossing: D2 has raids, TFD does not, the bosses are like (at least on normal mode) manageable, in particular if strong players carry the others. Even in normal mode, they are a challenge if no one carries. I personally dislike the convoluted raid mechanics in D2. In TFD hard mode bossing requires some knowledge on the bosses and if you play well, they go down - otherwise you will wipe mind that. However, that is not annoying to me like the D2 raids, but kind of satisfyinga and way less time consuming.

Loot: Grind is hard in all three games (yes, the grind in WF is atrocious, it just gives you lots of stuff in the beginning), however, as the combat in TFD is highly enjoyable which makes the grind enjoyable and relaxing. Important is that your strategy in terms of loadouts and mission selection makes the difference between "weeks" and "days" and "impossible" to "kindergarden"

Story:/Characters Well the story is freacking awful in all games D2 caters a certain immature audience in terms of certain characters. TFD has some quite dark moments in the story, be prepared for that, in particular, the voice acting contributes to that at these points. The English voice acting in TFD is simply very well done. TFD features attractive females (and males) with appropriate(!) fan service. D2 and WF do not embrace this concept of attractiveness or fan service to a degree where it would be worth mentioning. TFD's production design is not as epic as the one of D2 and not as mysterious and odd as the one of WF. I clearly like the enemy models in TFD more than the ones in WF.

Graphics /Sound: TFD is Unreal 5 (I think) it simply looks great. D2 and WF cannot compete with that. Sound is en par , except for as mentioned before, the voice acting in TFD is superior. 

Gunplay: WF has the worst weapon feeling EVER of any game I have played - hell, Duke Nukem 3Ds gunplay is better. In TFD, you "feel" it when you fire a gun and hit a target. I would say the gunplay of TFD and D2 are on a par.

In my opinion, all three games are hallmarks of the gerne, play them all to a certain extent. However, TFD is my favorite in many ways:
- shooter focused
- attractive characters and fan service
- no annoying raids but fulfilling boss fights

I don't mind a grind in a looter shooter, but this game takes it to a new horrible level. The drop rates for things is almost impossible there by forcing you to buy new characters just to try out something new. And the bosses get to the point of being impossible unless you have help, but if no one is in that area you have to wait. Not to mention the leveling of the weapons you almost have to up your weapon every three levels just to be able to handle the mobs. Not to mention the game favors one character over all the others in ability and power but even then make her one of the weakest when it comes to def, Unless you like a very long and hard grind I would not recommend this game at all, I made a more detailed review here if you would like to watch
